title: One Point Lesson - Tube Side Cleaning (Hydrojetting) (OPL-EA-5601-01)
content:
ONE POINT LESSON (OPL): OPL-EA-5601-01 - Tube Side Cleaning (Hydrojetting).

Equipment: EA-5601, Discipline: Mechanical, Area: 5600 - SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM.

References: Interlock: N/A (control loop only), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-5601.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains tube side cleaning (hydrojetting) for EA-5601 (SOLVENT HEATER) in the SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM. Hexane fouling on the tube side raises the differential pressure (PDT-5605) and cuts the heat duty, leaving cold solvent downstream. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Apply LOTO (Lock-Out Tag-Out) and prove zero energy before starting work.
- Precaution 2: Isolate, depressurise, drain and purge the equipment; obtain a valid work permit.
- Precaution 3: Wear the correct PPE: coverall, safety shoes, gloves, goggles and hearing protection.
- Precaution 4: Beware of stored mechanical energy (springs, rotating inertia) and pinch points.
- Precaution 5: Use certified lifting gear and correct manual-handling technique for heavy parts.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Standard mechanical hand tools & calibrated torque wrench
- Tool 2: LOTO padlocks and permit
- Tool 3: Laser/dial alignment kit (as applicable)
- Tool 4: Feeler gauges, dial indicator, seal/bearing pullers
- Tool 5: Correct spare parts and gaskets per the BOM
- Tool 6: Lifting gear and slings (certified)

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Isolate the solvent side and purge with nitrogen, remove channel covers
- Step 1 - Check: Isolation & LOTO verified
- Step 2 - Action: Hydrojet the 246 tubes (19.05 mm) to remove fouling
- Step 2 - Check: Parts match BOM / spec
- Step 3 - Action: Inspect tubes for corrosion or pitting
- Step 3 - Check: Torque / clearance to spec
- Step 4 - Action: Verify tube-side dP restored and no residual blockage
- Step 4 - Check: No leak / smooth operation
- Step 5 - Action: Re-gasket with new SW SS316 gasket and box up to torque
- Step 5 - Check: Record in equipment history

COMMON PROBLEMS & TROUBLESHOOTING:
- Symptom: High tube dP PDT-5605, low solvent outlet temperature | Cause: Hexane fouling / polymer fines deposit on tube bores | Action: Hydrojetted 246 tubes, restored dP and duty, re-gasketed
- Symptom: Hexane weep at channel flange | Cause: Spiral-wound channel gasket relaxed / damaged | Action: Renewed channel gasket, re-torqued in cross pattern
- Symptom: Continuous steam at condensate, high steam use | Cause: Steam trap element failed open | Action: Replaced steam trap element, verified condensate temperature

KEY LEARNING POINTS:
- Point 1: Hexane fouling on the tube side raises the differential pressure (PDT-5605) and cuts the heat duty, leaving cold solvent downstream.
- Point 2: Always cross-check the Datasheet limits and the P&ID TJC-LLD-PID-5601 before working on EA-5601.
- Point 3: Record the work in the equipment history so the Knowledge Hub stays the single source of truth.

Equipment: EA-5601, Discipline: Process / Operations, Area: 5600 - SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM.

References: Interlock: N/A (control loop only), P&ID: TJC-LLD-PID-5601.

PURPOSE & OBJECTIVE:
This One Point Lesson explains steam trap health check for EA-5601 (SOLVENT HEATER) in the SOLVENT HEATING SYSTEM. A failed steam trap either floods the shell (killing duty) or blows live steam (wasting energy); regular checks catch both. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

SAFETY PRECAUTIONS:
- Precaution 1: Obtain the correct operating permit and brief the shift team before the task.
- Precaution 2: Confirm hazardous fluids are isolated / inerted as required by procedure.
- Precaution 3: Beware of flammable, hot, or high-pressure fluids; wear the correct PPE.
- Precaution 4: Never defeat a safety interlock or trip without an authorised override permit.
- Precaution 5: Have emergency actions and communications ready before starting.

TOOLS & MATERIALS:
- Tool 1: Operating procedure & P&ID
- Tool 2: Radio / communication with panel
- Tool 3: Gas detector (O2 / LEL) as required
- Tool 4: Correct PPE for the fluid handled
- Tool 5: Sample containers & PPE for sampling
- Tool 6: Permit-to-work documentation

STEP-BY-STEP PROCEDURE:
- Step 1 - Action: Compare the condensate temperature TI-5604 to steam temperature
- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed
- Step 2 - Action: Use ultrasonic or a listening stick to check trap operation
- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit
- Step 3 - Action: A cold trap means flooding; a continuously hot blow means leak-through
- Step 3 - Check: Interlock status confirmed
- Step 4 - Action: Check the condensate pot level gauge LG-5606
- Step 4 - Check: Change logged on DCS
- Step 5 - Action: Replace the trap element or trap as required
- Step 5 - Check: Handover to next shift

- Symptom: Continuous steam at condensate, high steam use | Cause: Steam trap element failed open | Action: Replaced steam trap element, verified condensate temperature

Admitting steam onto a cold tube bundle too fast cracks the tube-to-tubesheet joints, causing internal leaks. The lesson gives operators and technicians the key knowledge and the correct step-by-step method so the task is done safely, correctly and consistently every time.

- Precaution 1: Obtain the correct operating permit and brief the shift team before the task.

- Step 1 - Check: Permit valid & briefed

- Step 2 - Check: Parameter within limit
- Step 3 - Action: Warm the exchanger through gradually
- Step 3 - Check: Interlock status confirmed
- Step 4 - Action: Avoid sudden large steps in the outlet temperature set-point
- Step 4 - Check: Change logged on DCS
- Step 5 - Action: Watch for knocking that indicates condensate hammer
- Step 5 - Check: Handover to next shift
